# lean-pkg page

render the README verification section from coverage.yaml, claims, the ledger and the receipts; stdout unless --write/--check/--out/--site/--html.

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg page [--write] [--check] [--out PATH] [--site DIR] [--html PATH] [--repo DIR]
              [--strict-preview] [--corroborate] [--attested] [--trusted-root FILE]
              [--allow-private-manuscript] [--agent AGENT] [--json] NAME
```

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` |   |
| `--write` | replace the marked block in the package README.md (append it when absent); prose outside the markers is untouched. For a gated package without lean-pkg-binding.yaml at the gated commit it then keeps the receipts bound through the deprecated registry route (when the record says nothing: `update NAME --accept-docs-descendants`, its own registry write; a record false is left alone), with a WARN, and writes lean-pkg-binding.yaml into the working tree (never staged or overwritten) to commit before the next verify run |
| `--check` | exit 1 when the README block is missing or stale, the lean-pkg credit is missing, or a site sentence has no backing receipt (or, for GitHub Actions, no corroborated run: --corroborate); with --site/--html also when those files are missing or stale; writes nothing |
| `--out PATH` | write the block here instead; README untouched |
| `--site DIR` | also write DIR/verification.md (the full page) and DIR/coverage.md (every row, its claims, inputs and notes) for MkDocs; with --check, compare them instead |
| `--html PATH` | also write one static HTML file (no script, no external asset) from the same data; with --check, compare it instead |
| `--repo DIR` | read the checkout DIR instead of the registered local_path, for this call only (never saved; for CI): DIR must be a git work tree, and when it has remotes one must be the package's repo; not with --write. Its committed HEAD is read: when the recorded gate receipt does not bind that HEAD (or an evidence-only descendant), the links and Lean statements are read at HEAD, no receipt fact is shown and the page says so; with --check, differences of such a preview from the receipt-bound files are warnings (exit 0) |
| `--strict-preview` | with --check --repo: a preview's differences from the receipt-bound README block and --site/--html files fail the check (exit 1) instead of warning |
| `--corroborate` | ask the public GitHub REST API about each GitHub Actions job coverage.yaml lists (level 2: the run, its job, the pinned verify.yml, the receipt annotation), and render the GitHub Actions sentence, with its run links, only when every one reaches it; a failure is named and fails closed. GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN, when set, only raises the rate limit and is never printed |
| `--attested` | verify each GitHub Actions job coverage.yaml lists at level 3: its committed Sigstore bundle (ci.attestation) with `gh attestation verify`, an optional outside tool, and the certificate against the ci block; the sentence renders at level 3, which holds after the run's records expire (with --corroborate too, level 2 must also hold); a failure is named |
| `--trusted-root FILE` | with --attested: verify offline against this Sigstore trusted root (gh attestation verify --custom-trusted-root) |
| `--allow-private-manuscript` | render against manuscript.version 'unposted'; the page then says so |
| `--agent AGENT` | with --write: the lease holder, when the package is leased |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `page NAME` | render the README verification section (status capsule, paper-to-Lean map, Not formalized, trust boundary, reproduce, evidence, citation, license, acknowledgments) between `<!-- lean-pkg:page:begin -->` and `<!-- lean-pkg:page:end -->` from `coverage.yaml`, `claims.yaml`, the claims ledger (a row is *verified* only when the ledger closes it) and the receipts committed under `.lean-receipts/` (allow-listed fields only); deterministic; the public-safety scanner runs over the block and a blocking hit refuses; stdout by default; `--write` replaces only the marked block in the package `README.md` (appends it when absent) and never commits; for a gated package without `lean-pkg-binding.yaml` at the gated commit it then keeps the receipts bound through the deprecated registry route (when the record says nothing: its own `update NAME --accept-docs-descendants` invocation, the one registry write; a record `false` is left alone), prints `WARN: deprecated: ...` (`--json` `deprecations[]`) and writes `lean-pkg-binding.yaml` into the working tree, never staged or overwritten (`--json` `binding_file` {path, state, written}), to commit on its own right before the next verify run ([the docs-only opt-in](../page.md#the-docs-only-opt-in)); with the file at that commit it does none of this; `--check` exits 1 when the block is missing or stale, the lean-pkg credit is missing, or the README mentions a site (the Easley Cluster, GitHub Actions) without a backing receipt, or the GitHub Actions sentence without a corroborated run; `--corroborate` asks the public GitHub REST API about each GitHub Actions job `coverage.yaml` lists (level 2, as `receipt check --corroborate`, against the registry's repository) and renders the GitHub Actions sentence, `{runs}` filled with the runs' links, only when every one reaches level 2; a failure is a warning naming why, and fails closed (`GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN` only raises the rate limit; JSON `sites.github-actions` gains `corroboration` {job: rows} and `runs[]`; [GitHub Actions](../sites.md#github-actions)); `--attested` verifies each listed job's committed Sigstore bundle with `gh attestation verify` (level 3, as `receipt check --attested`; `--trusted-root FILE` offline), so the sentence renders after the run's records expire, and `sites.<name>.level`/`levels` reach 3 (with `--corroborate` too, level 3 needs both answers); toolchain advisory lines (`- Toolchain advisory: ...`, one per entry of lean-pkg's toolchain advisories list naming the gate receipt's toolchain) are left out of that comparison, so a new advisory never makes a page stale: `--check` prints a non-failing `NOTE: toolchain advisory ID applies; the next page --write will show it` instead, and `--json` lists `toolchain_advisories[]`; `--out PATH` writes the block elsewhere; `--site DIR` also writes `DIR/verification.md` (the full page) and `DIR/coverage.md` (every row with its claims, declarations, ledger statuses, inputs and notes) for MkDocs, and `--html PATH` one static HTML file of both (no script, no external asset); with `--check` those files are compared instead (missing or stale: exit 1); user text is escaped in every output; `--repo DIR` reads that checkout instead of `local_path` for this call (CI; not with `--write`), at its committed HEAD: when the recorded gate receipt does not bind that HEAD (or an evidence-only descendant), the file links and Lean statements are read at HEAD, no receipt fact (axioms, `sorry` count, statement comparison, the receipt used) is shown, a `Preview of commit` note names both commits, and JSON `repo_override` gains `head`, `anchor_commit` and `receipt_facts` {receipt, commit, included, binds_head, reason}; with `--check` on such a preview, its differences from the receipt-bound README block and `--site`/`--html` files are warnings (exit 0, JSON `preview: true`, `current: null`) while real problems still exit 1, and `--strict-preview` (only with `--check --repo`; otherwise exit 2) makes them fail; `--json` gains `preview`, `site_files[]` {path, status} and `repo_override` ([The verification page](../page.md)) | `[--write \| --check \| --out PATH]` `[--site DIR]` `[--html PATH]` `[--repo DIR]` `[--strict-preview]` `[--corroborate]` `[--attested [--trusted-root FILE]]` `[--allow-private-manuscript]` `[--agent A]` |

## Exit codes

0 success (dry runs and no-ops included), 1 refused or failed, 2 usage error; see [Exit codes](../cli.md#exit-codes).

## JSON output

Top-level keys of `--json`, as recorded in the golden contract (tests/golden/json-keys.json):

- `page` (exit 0): `counts`, `current`, `easley`, `kind`, `ledger_digest`, `ledger_status`, `manuscript`, `markdown`, `name`, `ok`, `preview`, `private_manuscript`, `problems`, `readme`, `receipts`, `repo_override`, `rows`, `site_files`, `sites`, `toolchain_advisories`, `unchanged`, `verified_rows`, `warnings`, `written`

## Examples

Print the README verification section rendered from coverage.yaml, the claims, the ledger and the receipts.

```bash
lean-pkg page my-proof
```

Replace the marked block in the package README.md (append it when absent). Without lean-pkg-binding.yaml at the gated commit it keeps the receipts bound through the deprecated registry route (a WARN) and writes that file into the working tree; commit README.md without it.

```bash
lean-pkg page my-proof --write
```

Exit 1 when the README block is missing or stale; a CI step for the package.

```bash
lean-pkg page my-proof --check
```

Also write the docs pages and one self-contained HTML file.

```bash
lean-pkg page my-proof --site docs --html docs/verification.html
```

The same check with each GitHub Actions run corroborated against the public run API, so the GitHub Actions sentence (with its run links) is earned; for CI, with GITHUB_TOKEN set.

```bash
lean-pkg page my-proof --check --corroborate
```

The same check with each GitHub Actions run's committed attestation verified by gh attestation verify (level 3), so the sentence stays earned after the run expires.

```bash
lean-pkg page my-proof --check --attested
```
